tweets.text:
It’s never been easier to make millions of dollars without having to spend years learning how to properly scout the biggest pain points, the desires, the needs of your audience you want to sell too.

I’ve secretly been using AI to help give me ideas and feedback of how IT thinks humans think.

My feedback is this…

I have used Claude for 3 internal promotions.

The first time I used Claude I gave it my current headlines, bullets, emails, etc. 

I asked for it to keep the same format and structure but give me a unique angle pertaining to my current headline/subject/bullet.

I actually asked for 5 after it gave me 1. One really stood out and Claude even said “this is the one that would perform the best” and it explains why.

Ironically that ANGLE for the same product I promoted the week before did 2x the numbers. 

I didn’t change anything except the angle and positioning. 

Needless to say, even with aff campaigns we’ve been taking creatives that are performing well, transcribing and asking Claude to make it better by doing XYZ (not giving my prompts).

Them tell it “do you think Facebook ads will approve this based on their ad policies” and it wil say something like “great point” and rewrite.

Needless to say.

The AI you use doesn’t really matter I think. I used ChatGPT but fell in love with Claude. 

There is a  massive market untapped…

Prompts.

If someone sold a $1,000 guide on prompts to copy and paste and prove the results they obtained from said prompts - would sell like crazy.

The problem we face is explaining to the AI what we are looking for and for it to follow exactly what you want. 

The video below is how I interact but typically I will go for 1 hour and refine and get it to REALLY think and deliver stuff I didn’t even think about. 

Use AI.

But don’t let it be your crutch. 

If you’re stupid and don’t know what converts or how to structure campaigns and angles nothing can help you. You gotta have some sort of “know how” of what converts and then tweak it to make it better or unique. 

- enjoy

New Claude release is very close - and it has „extreme reasoning“!

Release in the next few weeks

Anthropic’s new Claude Sonnet and Opus models introduce a dynamic loop between reasoning and tool use. They don’t just answer—they pause, reassess, and course-correct if stuck, merging autonomous action with deep contextual reflection.

This evolution in model architecture pushes AI toward more adaptive, less supervised systems—bringing us closer to agents that reason like collaborators, not calculators. It’s a leap toward truly intelligent, self-correcting systems that could power future breakthroughs across research, code, and beyond.

"For people who use the new models to generate code, the models will automatically test the code they created to make sure it’s running correctly. If there’s a mistake, the models can stop to think about what might have gone wrong and then correct it."

tweets.text:
The thing i like the most about Claude Code is that i can easily see everything passed to the model, so it's easy to improve my own mental model of the model.
Cursor, on the other hand, has too many unknown which makes it harder to do so.
Max mode is great but still has some issues:
1. it manipulates the context i provided via @

2. i can't tell what tools the model used to make edit to a file.  (in claude code i can use this information to help model make better decisions)

It's trivial to prompt the model to give me these information. So i think Cursor can simply expose these information as a debug mode or something. 
cc @mntruell
